claims.text: Increasing the density of uniformly distributed coherent nanoprecipitates in high-entropy-alloy coatings improves wear performance.
Coherent nanoprecipitates enable controlled dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitates reduce stress concentrations at the coating surface.
A controlled aging or minor-element-alloying treatment can induce coherent nanoprecipitates within an HEA coating.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote a more uniform stress distribution.
Coherent nanoprecipitates reduce localized deformation during abrasive and adhesive wear.
Stress relief associated with coherent nanoprecipitates reduces crack initiation during wear.
Controlled dislocation flow minimizes material removal and wear-debris formation.
Untreated homogeneous HEA coatings are more prone to stress concentrations than precipitate-containing coatings.
A coating containing induced coherent nanoprecipitates will have a lower wear rate than the untreated baseline.
A coating containing induced coherent nanoprecipitates will exhibit more stable friction behavior than the untreated baseline.
A coating containing induced coherent nanoprecipitates will show less surface degradation, including lower roughness and reduced wear debris.
The proposed mechanism should dominate only in regimes where processing reliably produces coherent nanoprecipitates.
Extreme temperature or wear load can reduce the benefit by causing precipitate coarsening, dissolution, or loss of coherency.
Compositions outside the optimal precipitate-formation window will show a diminished wear benefit.
